title: has() rejects field selection off a map literal
body: Calling has() on a field selection off a map literal raises an error instead of reporting whether the key is present. For example, has({}.a) raises an error rather than returning false, and has({"a": 1}.a) raises the same error rather than returning true. The equivalent membership expression using the in operator already works correctly for both the empty and the populated map: "a" in {} returns false, and "a" in {"a": 1} returns true. has() should behave the same way when its argument is a map-valued expression, not only when it is rooted in a plain variable name. Please make has() return the correct boolean for a map literal receiver instead of raising an error.

title: Registered cross-type equality overload is inconsistently honored
body: After registering a custom operator that defines how a string date value should compare equal to a timestamp value returned by a function, the direct equality expression between the two honors the registered operator correctly. However, using the same string date as a list element and checking whether the corresponding timestamp value is a member of that list with the in operator reports not-equal, and comparing two single-element lists for equality (one holding the string date, the other holding the timestamp value) also reports not-equal. Both of these should honor the same registered operator that the direct equality expression already does, since they are all just different ways of asking whether the two values are equal. Please make membership checks and list equality consistently consult a registered cross-type equality operator instead of assuming values of different types can never be equal.
